react.initialize: await warmUpEngine() in an effect before creating a World, DrawingDocument or procedural geometry (required in the browser)
react.keyboard: createKeyboardInput(surfaceElement, { mode: 'pointer' | 'drag' | 'swipe', enabled }) maps arrows/WASD/Space/Enter to the same pointer gestures; browser only; dispose() on unmount

reactNative.surface: Native development build; Expo Go does not include the engine
reactNative.assets: Metro require(...) numbers or URI strings
reactNative.initialize: await warmUpEngine() (synchronous on native; built-in shapes also work before it); rebuild the app after native engine changes

fileStructure.gameConstants.ts: Tuning numbers, colors, asset sources and an async loadAssets()
fileStructure.game.ts: createGame(): World, camera, rules, start/stop/reset/update/tap/dispose; no React, DOM or react-native imports
fileStructure.useGame.ts: React hook: await warmUpEngine(), createGame() in an effect, dispose in cleanup, ignore late setup after unmount
fileStructure.GamePage.tsx | GameScreen.tsx: One host screen: GameView, HUD text and buttons

lifecycleRules: Create the World inside a React effect after await warmUpEngine(); never during render, in useMemo or at module scope.
Call world.update(dt) exactly once per frame, from GameView onUpdate only.
If you queue moves on world.transforms, call world.transforms.flush() once at the end of onUpdate, after world.update(dt). It is not flushed automatically.
Call world.dispose() in the effect cleanup and cancel async setup that finishes after unmount.

Use world.isDisposed instead of your own flag. After dispose, despawn/set/has/animate/stopAnimation/impulse/playClip/stopClip/after/cancelTimer/cancelTimers/queries/forEachCollision are safe no-ops; spawn, update, burst and effects throw.
workflow: Initialize once per scene, after warmUpEngine.
Store gameplay in a shared TypeScript factory returning world, camera, update and input functions.
Connect one world.update(dt) to GameView.onUpdate; queue per-frame moves on world.transforms and flush once after update.
Use React state only for HUD changes (score, seconds, status), never for per-frame transforms.
Define round start, stop, reset and a once-only result report in the game layer.
Ready screen: world.scoreboard.reset(lives, countdownSeconds); start with world.scoreboard.resume().
On pause, stop updates and input; on reset, cancel timers, despawn round actors, clear input and reset the scoreboard.
Prepare assets outside the frame loop; async model, texture, font and sound loaders initialize the core and reuse resources automatically.
Cancel late asynchronous setup and dispose the world on unmount.

api.create: new World(capacity)  // capacity covers entities, text letters and particles
api.change: world.set(entity, options)  // returns false if gone or disposed
api.moveEveryFrame: world.transforms.position(e, x, y, z) | rotation(e, qx, qy, qz, qw) | scale(e, x, y?, z?) | color(e, r, g, b, a?) | transform(e, x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw); then world.transforms.flush()
api.rotate: quat.y(angle) | quat.x | quat.z | quat.axisAngle(x, y, z, angle) | quat.fromEuler(x, y, z) | quat.multiply(a, b) (a after b) | quat.slerp(a, b, t) | quat.identity; every helper takes an optional out MutableQuat
api.queriesWithOut: world.position(e, out) | worldPosition(e, out) | velocity(e, out) | raycast(origin, dir, max, mask, outHit) | pick(x, y, outHit) | toScreen(p, out) | screenToWorld(x, y, plane, out)
api.screenQueriesBeforeFirstFrame: toScreen and screenToWorld return null until a frame has been drawn
api.effects: effects.confetti | sparkle | shatter | splash | sparks | explosion (world, EffectOptions) ; effects.dust(world, DustOptions) ; effects.flash(world, FlashOptions)
api.effectOptions: { position, colors, size, speed, count, lifetime, gravity?, direction?, spread?, flash? }
api.popClearedPiece: await effects.pop(world, piece, { scale, color?, flash?, delay?, duration? }); world.despawn(piece)  // default duration effects.POP_TIME
api.glowColors: effects.hot(color, peak?, alpha?) ; effects.pale(color, t, alpha?)
api.readyScreen: world.scoreboard.reset(lives, countdownSeconds)  // stopped full countdown; resume() starts it
api.soundSettings: audio.enabled = settings.enableSounds  // inverse of audio.muted; mirrors haptics.enabled
api.meshLimit: MAX_MESHES = 4096 mesh ids including 16 built-in shapes; ids are never freed, so never create meshes per spawn
api.colors: GameView background and Light.color accept Color (RGB or RGBA; alpha ignored)
api.assetSource: AssetSource = string | number; URLs on React, Metro require(...) or URIs on React Native
api.types: Import GameViewProps, GameViewStats, JoystickProps, AssetSource, AudioPlayOptions, ClipOptions, ScreenPlane, GeometryPart, ParametricSurfaceOptions, EffectOptions, DustOptions, FlashOptions, PopOptions, MutableQuat, TransformBatch, DrawingStroke, DrawingSample and DrawingCoverageOptions.
api.meshIdScanLimit: getMeshIdLimit(); exclusive upper bound, not a mesh count
api.path: new Path().addRoundedRect(x, y, width, height, radius); quadraticTo and toContours use descriptive names.

drawing.create: await warmUpEngine(); const doc = new DrawingDocument(width, height, pixelRatio?)  // one per screen, in an effect
drawing.tools: doc.setBrush({ brushType, color, width, opacity, pressure?, smoothing?, isEraser?, symmetry? }) ; doc.updateControls({ tool, color, width, ... }) ; doc.undo() / redo() / clear() return DrawingState
drawing.saveLoad: doc.exportProject() / doc.load(project) ; doc.exportSVG() ; doc.snapshot() -> { base64, width, height } ; doc.captureDraft(revision) for autosave
drawing.gameTexture: world.spawn({ mesh: "plane", texture: doc.texture() })  // live; freed by doc.dispose()
drawing.gameInput: doc.input(phase 0 begin | 1 move | 2 end | 3 cancel, x, y, pressure, 'document')  // always end or cancel a begun stroke
drawing.strokes: doc.strokes({ from, tolerance }) -> DrawingStroke[] (index, bounds, lines centrelines, outline contours)
drawing.coverage: doc.coverage({ x, y, width, height, minAlpha }) -> 0..1
drawing.lifecycle: clear() on replay; dispose() on unmount (after the world). Unlike World, a disposed document throws: check doc.isDisposed.

neverDo: Create a World during render, in useMemo or at module scope.
Call world.update more than once per frame or from requestAnimationFrame/setInterval.
Queue on world.transforms without calling flush().
Store per-frame positions or velocities in React state.
Use setTimeout/setInterval for gameplay delays (use world.after).
Keep a custom disposed flag (use world.isDisposed).
Spawn entities or fire effects on a disposed world.
Allocate arrays/objects per frame in hot paths (use out arguments).
Hand-build particle layers when an effects.* call exists.
Create meshes per spawn or inside onUpdate.
Invent entity IDs or API names; check the API reference.
Test React Native in Expo Go.

distinctions.entity: A handle for one object in one World
distinctions.model: A reusable mesh; spawn entities from it
distinctions.pause: Stop updates and input while retaining the current world
distinctions.reset: Application function that prepares a fresh round
distinctions.time: dt and animation/timer durations are in seconds
distinctions.coordinates: World Y is up; ground movement uses X/Z. Screen input is local view points or CSS pixels.
distinctions.rotation: Quaternion [x, y, z, w]; build with quat; angles in radians

verification: Typecheck the shared game code against each requested host (e.g. bunx tsc --noEmit -p .).
The game surface has a real size.
Start, score, win, lose, stop (cancel), replay and unmount work; each run reports one result.
Input and clock do not advance while paused.
Web assets load from the built host over HTTP(S).
Only claim native runtime verification after exercising a native development build.

performance.zeroAllocation: Reuse out arguments for queries, quat out arrays and world.transforms scalar methods so frames allocate nothing.
performance.batching: world.transforms merges updates per entity and applies them in one native call per flush.
performance.web: The browser renderer reads world output buffers in place in WASM memory; JS mirrors copy only valid instances.
performance.drawing: Undo/redo and layer replay reuse composite buffers in one pass; only changed texture rows upload.

caching.automatic: Rust owns shape hashing, preparation, solid generation and prepared-mesh caching. Loaders also persist original asset bytes through the Rust cache.
caching.persistence: No TTL or automatic eviction. Native uses app-private Application Support/filesDir storage without expo-file-system. Web uses binary IndexedDB records with a browser-managed quota; files load on demand and recent prepared geometry warms into Rust.
caching.fallback: Denied/full storage or corrupt records cause a rebuild; completed records are not evicted to make room.
caching.ownership: Create a new World and fresh entities per scene. Dispose worlds on unmount; shared assets remain valid.
caching.advanced: ProceduralCache(revision) is optional for expensive deterministic multi-model factories.
caching.clear: await clearAssetCache() from an explicit user action; clears engine-owned saved assets while preserving loaded worlds/handles and unrelated app data.
caching.gamesIntegration: @nayan-ui/games heavy-game loaders await engine initialization before builders. The library needs no expo-file-system cache adapter; factory caches retain recipe identity and skip JS construction. Game components still require their React Native host.

assetLoading.initialize: loadModel, loadTexture, loadFont and audio.load initialize the core automatically; no application readiness cache is required.
assetLoading.errors: Model, texture and font loading rejects with the API name, source and original Error.cause; sound bank failures log and skip optional sounds. Retry by calling the loader again.
assetLoading.ownership: Loaded handles are session resources shared across worlds. Each scene owns and disposes its own World. clearAssetCache removes saved data without invalidating loaded handles.
